summary_html: A **parent/guardian/child requests help** without a substantiated allegation. FFPSA created a federal pathway for **prevention services** to avert removal and stabilize families before a case escalates.
authority_html: - **Family First Prevention Services Act (2018)** — prevention services, kinship support; shifts upstream from removal to support

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: JET v. State, Department of Family Services
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the refusal to let a young mother withdraw her admission of neglect, holding the juvenile court gave the statutorily required advisements at the initial hearing and did not abuse its discretion despite her claim of mental illness and her own earlier requests for help.
key_cases.relevance: The mother had sought help voluntarily from public-health and counseling services before the petition was filed, and the Court declined to treat that as a reason to undo the adjudication.
key_cases.quote: The juvenile court did not abuse its discretion in denying the appellant's motion to withdraw her admission of neglect

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The plurality held Washington's breathtakingly broad grandparent visitation statute unconstitutional as applied, because it gave no special weight to a fit parent's decision, and reaffirmed the presumption that fit parents act in their children's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: When a parent asks for help rather than being accused, the constitutional presumption that the parent is acting in the child's interests still governs state responses.
key_cases.quote: there is a presumption that fit parents act in the best interests of their children

key_cases.holding: Applying Troxel, the Court held Wyoming's grandparent visitation statute must be read to require grandparents to prove by clear and convincing evidence that the parents are unfit or that their visitation decisions are or will be harmful before any best-interests inquiry, and affirmed denial of the grandparents' petition.
key_cases.relevance: Confirms that a fit parent's own decisions about a child's care and contacts are entitled to constitutional deference when third parties seek state intervention.
key_cases.quote: Parents have a fundamental due process right to guide the upbringing of their children, including determining the level of contact with their grandparents

state_agency.name: Wyoming Department of Family Services
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the DFS field office in the county where the child lives — the list is at dfs.wyo.gov/about/contact-us

mandatory_reporters: Any person (universal mandatory reporting) — Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-205(a)

Staff of a medical or other public or private institution, school, facility or agency must also notify the person in charge, who is then also responsible for making the report — Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-205(b)

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Notification of a suspected case of child abuse or neglect
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in statute; Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-204(a)(iii) states the duty without a penalty, and the agency must seek a court order if denied reasonable access to the child

parent_rights_at_moment: Right to refuse entry without warrant
Right to be advised of the specific complaints or allegations against you at the initial time of contact (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-204(a)(iii))
A DFS caseworker cannot take your child: only a law enforcement officer, a treating physician, physician's assistant or nurse practitioner, or a court order can (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-405)
what_to_say: I do not consent to entry without a warrant
Please provide your card and the allegations in writing
I will have my attorney contact you
what_not_to_do: Do not let them in 'just to look'
